question: How can datasets, elementary machine learning, and interpretation be organized into a reproducible discovery loop that yields precise structures and conjectures about mathematical objects rather than only accurate predictions?

key_findings.claim: The article defines mathematical data science as a four-stage loop from mathematical objects to data, exploratory models, interpretation, and exact mathematics.
key_findings.evidence: Objects are embedded as finite feature vectors with targets, supervised or unsupervised tools test for collective structure, and model internals or summary statistics are translated back into named invariants, conjectures, sufficient conditions, or theorems. The authors stress that representation and sampling choices are part of the mathematics, not neutral preprocessing.

key_findings.claim: Short sequences of Frobenius traces strongly predict elliptic-curve rank, and simple averaging reveals an oscillatory rank-conditioned structure called murmuration.
key_findings.evidence: The case study represents each curve by the first 300 prime-indexed traces a_p. Logistic regression on 16,000 rank-0 and 16,000 rank-1 curves below conductor 10,000 reaches nearly 99% accuracy. PCA separates ranks, but directly averaging a_p within conductor windows exposes oscillations whose shape changes with rank and conductor scale.

key_findings.claim: The elliptic-curve result is a discovery narrative, not evidence that prediction accuracy alone proves a new mathematical law.
key_findings.evidence: The oscillation became mathematically useful only after replacing opaque classification success with rank-conditioned averages, testing conductor windows and other families, and connecting the plots to later theoretical work on modular-form murmurations. The article supplies selected experiments rather than a preregistered or held-out discovery protocol.

key_findings.claim: Kronecker-coefficient positivity is highly predictable from partition triples, but the useful mathematical output comes from interpretable spectral loadings.
key_findings.evidence: For n=12,13,14, nearest neighbors, 2D/3D CNNs, and LightGBM classify zero versus nonzero coefficients, with best accuracies 0.9714, 0.9837, and 0.9845. PCA-inspired similarity and L1-difference matrices define a- and b-loadings from leading eigenvectors, producing scalar coordinates on partitions and triples.

key_findings.claim: The b-loading yields an explicit nonvanishing certificate for a substantial subset of partition triples.
key_findings.evidence: With b* defined as the minimum b-loading among known zero coefficients, b(t)<b* immediately implies g(t) is nonzero. At n=20, 78,382,890 of 246,491,883 triples—about 31.8%—satisfy the certificate; the authors conjecture that this fraction has positive infimum in the large-n limit.

anchors.section: 3.6 Distributions conditioned on g(t) nonzero or zero

key_findings.claim: Negative model results and high accuracy both require restraint because finite sampling and feature design can create or hide apparent structure.
key_findings.evidence: The conclusion explicitly says 99% is only a screening signal, recommends simple methods for interpretation, and warns that a failed experiment may reflect the chosen finite subset, size parameter, distribution, or representation. Neither case study derives statistical uncertainty for the discovery-selection process or guards against repeated exploratory testing.

method.core_idea: Study families of mathematical objects as datasets, use predictive success only to locate structure, and translate the simplest stable statistical patterns back into exact mathematical definitions and statements.
method.mechanism: Choose a finite sampling regime and numerical representation; train elementary supervised models or compute PCA/covariance summaries; inspect coefficients, eigenvectors, averages, and conditional distributions; define new invariants such as murmurations or spectral loadings; then test and formalize resulting sufficient conditions and conjectures with ordinary mathematics.
assumptions: A finite sample is representative of the mathematical family and asymptotic regime of interest.
Chosen numeric features retain the structure relevant to the target question.
Stable model behavior reflects mathematical regularity rather than sampling artifacts or leakage.
Statistical summaries can be converted into exact definitions that remain meaningful beyond the training range.

techniques.role: Encodes families of curves or partitions as finite numerical samples with explicit targets and size regimes.
Uses logistic regression, nearest neighbors, CNNs, or LightGBM to test whether a representation contains recoverable structure.
Turns leading covariance directions into visible oscillations or spectral coordinates.
Replaces a classifier with rank-conditioned Frobenius-trace averages that expose murmurations.
Defines a- and b-loadings from leading eigenvectors and derives a sufficient nonvanishing criterion.

evaluations.setting: 32,000 elliptic curves of ranks 0 and 1 with conductors 1–10,000 and 300 prime traces
evaluations.result: Nearly 99% accuracy; accuracy remains high with fewer trace coefficients and for three-rank experiments.
evaluations.baseline: Rank prior and reduced-feature variants described narratively

evaluations.setting: Balanced elliptic-curve datasets over several conductor windows
evaluations.metric: PCA separation and averaged Frobenius-trace curves
evaluations.result: PC1 separates ranks and rank-conditioned trace averages show conductor-dependent oscillatory murmuration patterns.
evaluations.baseline: Unconditioned/simple trace representation and alternative conductor windows

evaluations.setting: Kronecker coefficient zero/nonzero prediction for n=12,13,14
evaluations.result: Best reported accuracies are 0.9714, 0.9837, and 0.9845, respectively, using LGBM or CNN3.
evaluations.baseline: Nearest neighbors, CNN2, CNN3, and LightGBM across input layouts

evaluations.result: 78,382,890 of 246,491,883 triples, approximately 31.8%, satisfy the sufficient condition.
evaluations.baseline: No certificate beyond direct Kronecker-coefficient computation

limitations: This is a perspective and two-case-study article, not a controlled benchmark of mathematical discovery methods.
Dataset construction, conductor windows, partition size, and feature encodings can change apparent patterns.
High interpolation accuracy does not establish an asymptotic theorem or causal mathematical mechanism.
Exploratory selection across many plots and models is not accompanied by multiple-testing or uncertainty analysis.
The b-loading threshold depends on knowledge of zero coefficients at a fixed n and its asymptotic coverage is conjectural.
Both successful examples rely on substantial expert interpretation and domain-specific computation.
failure_modes: Train/test leakage through shared size, conductor, or isomorphism structure can create spurious accuracy.
A finite-range oscillation can disappear or change after rescaling to another asymptotic regime.
An interpretable principal component can still be a sampling artifact rather than an invariant.
Optimizing prediction may favor a representation that obscures the simplest exact mathematics.
A negative result may incorrectly terminate a promising direction because the wrong features or sample distribution were chosen.
reusable_insights: Treat predictive accuracy as a structure detector, not the scientific endpoint.
After a complex model succeeds, search for the simplest statistic that reproduces its separation.
Record sampling regimes and rescale plots across size parameters before asserting an asymptotic pattern.
Require a machine-discovered quantity to become an exact, independently checkable definition or statement.
Reserve fresh mathematical ranges for confirmation after exploratory feature and model selection.
open_questions: How should mathematical discovery pipelines control adaptive exploration and multiple comparisons?
Which stability tests distinguish finite-sample visual patterns from asymptotic invariants?
Can models automatically propose human-readable exact formulas from stable spectral directions?
What independent benchmarks can compare the rate of genuinely new conjectures and proofs rather than prediction accuracy?
Can the positive-coverage conjecture for the b-loading certificate be proved or strengthened?

competitive_landscape.title: Murmurations of Elliptic Curves
competitive_landscape.difference: The source paper gives the elliptic-curve datasets, rank prediction, and averaged Frobenius-trace phenomenon in detail. The reviewed article abstracts that episode into a general discovery workflow and pairs it with a representation-theory case.

competitive_landscape.title: Data-scientific Study of Kronecker Coefficients
competitive_landscape.difference: Lee develops the partition loadings and nonvanishing criterion technically. The reviewed article is a higher-level synthesis emphasizing how predictive experiments were translated into exact mathematical structure.

competitive_landscape.title: Murmurations
competitive_landscape.difference: Zubrilina proves a related correlation phenomenon for Fourier coefficients and root numbers of modular-form families. It exemplifies the proof stage that the reviewed workflow seeks but does not itself provide a general data-science methodology.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine Learning Meets Algebraic Combinatorics: A Suite of Datasets Capturing Research-level Conjecturing Ability in Pure Mathematics
competitive_landscape.difference: ACD Repo standardizes nine research-level algebraic-combinatorics datasets and explicitly targets conjecturing evaluation. Douglas and Lee instead present a methodological essay with two retrospective discoveries and no cross-method benchmark.

competitive_landscape.title: Murmurations of Modular Forms and p-power Coefficients
competitive_landscape.difference: Kundu and Mueller extend the proved/observed murmuration program to prime-power-indexed coefficients. This strengthens the phenomenon's mathematical reach but is narrower than the reviewed article's general claim about data-driven discovery.

novelty_assessment: The article's novelty is primarily synthesis and pedagogy: it names and operationalizes a mathematical-data-science loop and connects two discoveries. The underlying elliptic-curve and Kronecker results appeared in earlier papers by the same research community. Its enduring value is the insistence that accuracy is a screening step and that success means an exact, human-readable mathematical object, while a rigorous discovery-validation protocol remains unspecified.
reviewer_notes: Read all 17 extracted pages, including the paradigm discussion, elliptic-curve construction and plots, Kronecker coefficient experiments, loading definitions, sufficient condition, and concluding methodological cautions. Primary arXiv records for both case-study sources, Zubrilina's theorem, and later dataset/extension work were checked on 2026-08-23. The review distinguishes retrospective narrative evidence from prospective validation of a discovery process.
